module_title: Refurbishing and Selling Used Auto Parts

lessons.title: Cleaning and testing used parts before sale
lessons.body: Before you sell any used part, you must clean it and test it. A dirty part looks like junk and won't fetch a good price. Start by scraping off heavy grease with a putty knife, then soak the part in a bucket of diesel or kerosene for 30 minutes. Use a wire brush to scrub away rust and dirt. For aluminium parts like alternator housings, use a brass wire brush to avoid scratching. After cleaning, rinse with water and dry with compressed air or a clean rag. For electrical parts like alternators and starters, testing is critical. You need a multimeter (cost: about 5,000-10,000 Naira or 300-600 KES). Set it to DC volts. For an alternator, spin the pulley by hand and check that the rotor turns freely without grinding. Connect the multimeter to the output terminal and spin the pulley with a drill; you should see 12-14 volts. For a starter, connect it to a 12V battery with jumper cables. The starter gear should jump out and spin strongly. If it just clicks or spins slowly, it's no good. For brake calipers, check that the piston moves in and out smoothly using a C-clamp. If it's stuck, it needs a rebuild. For mechanical parts like steering racks or driveshafts, check for excessive play by wiggling joints. Any part that fails testing should be sold as scrap metal, not as a used part. Keep a testing log: write the part name, test result, and date. This helps you price accurately and avoid returns. Remember, a clean, tested part can sell for 3-5 times more than an untested, dirty one. In many African markets, buyers trust you more if you show them the test results. So invest in a multimeter and a battery charger; they pay for themselves quickly.

lessons.title: Basic repairs: rebuilding alternators, starters, and brake calipers
lessons.body: Rebuilding alternators, starters, and brake calipers can double or triple your profit. Start with alternators. Most failures are worn brushes, bad bearings, or a faulty voltage regulator. Buy a rebuild kit (brushes, bearings, regulator) for about 3,000-5,000 Naira or 200-400 KES. Disconnect the battery, remove the alternator, and open the casing. Take photos as you go. Replace the brushes if they are less than 5mm long. Press out old bearings with a socket and hammer, then tap in new ones gently. Clean the slip rings with fine sandpaper (400 grit). Solder new brushes in place. Reassemble and test: spin by hand, then with a drill, and check voltage output. For starters, common issues are worn solenoid contacts, bad brushes, and dirty commutator. A starter rebuild kit costs 2,500-4,000 Naira or 150-300 KES. Open the starter, clean the commutator with sandpaper, undercut the mica if needed, and replace brushes and solenoid contacts. Test with a battery: the gear should kick out and spin fast. For brake calipers, the main problem is a stuck piston due to rust. Buy a caliper rebuild kit (new seals and dust boots) for 1,500-3,000 Naira or 100-200 KES. Remove the piston using compressed air (careful: it can fly out). Clean the bore with brake cleaner and a hone. Replace seals, lubricate with brake grease, and reassemble. Test by pumping the piston out with a brake pedal or air. Always use new brake fluid when installing. Rebuilding requires patience and cleanliness. Work on a clean bench, use the right tools (snap ring pliers, torque wrench), and never reuse old seals. Sell rebuilt parts with a 30-day warranty. In many African cities, rebuilt alternators sell for 15,000-25,000 Naira or 1,000-1,500 KES, while starters go for 12,000-20,000 Naira or 800-1,200 KES. Calipers fetch 8,000-15,000 Naira or 500-900 KES. That's good money for a few hours of work.

lessons.title: Pricing used parts based on condition and demand
lessons.body: Pricing used parts is not guesswork. You need to consider condition, demand, and the price of new parts. Start by grading each part: A (like new, tested, clean), B (good, minor wear, works), C (usable but needs repair), D (for scrap only). Grade A parts can sell for 50-70% of new price. Grade B for 30-50%. Grade C for 10-25%. Grade D for scrap value by weight. For example, a new alternator for a Toyota Corolla might cost 60,000 Naira or 4,000 KES. A Grade A used one can sell for 30,000-40,000 Naira or 2,000-2,800 KES. A Grade B for 18,000-30,000 Naira or 1,200-2,000 KES. Check online platforms like Jiji, OLX, or Facebook Marketplace to see what others are asking. But don't just copy prices; adjust for your part's condition. Demand matters: parts for popular models like Toyota, Honda, Nissan, and Hyundai sell faster and for higher prices. Rare models may sit for months, so price lower to move them. Also consider urgency: if a mechanic needs a part today, they'll pay more. Offer a small discount for bulk buys (e.g., 10% off for 5+ parts). Keep a record of what you paid for the scrap car and what you've sold from it. Your goal is to recover the car's cost within the first 5-10 parts sold, then everything else is profit. For example, if you bought a scrap Corolla for 150,000 Naira or 10,000 KES, selling the alternator, starter, gearbox, and ECU might already cover that. Don't be afraid to negotiate, but know your bottom line. A good rule: never sell below your cost plus 20% for Grade A and B parts. For Grade C, sell at cost or slightly above to clear space. Use a pricing sheet: list part, grade, new price, your price, and date sold. Review monthly and adjust.

lessons.title: Marketing parts to local mechanics and online platforms
lessons.body: Marketing is how you turn parts into cash. Start with local mechanics. Visit at least 10 mechanics within a 5km radius. Bring a notebook with your parts list and prices. Introduce yourself, hand out a simple business card (name, phone, what you sell). Offer a 5-10% commission for any mechanic who brings you a buyer. Mechanics talk to each other, so one good relationship can bring many sales. Also visit auto electricians, panel beaters, and tyre shops. For online platforms, use Jiji, OLX, Facebook Marketplace, and WhatsApp groups. Take clear photos: clean the part, place it on a plain background (like a white cloth), and take photos from multiple angles. Include a ruler or coin for scale. Write a detailed title: e.g., 'Toyota Corolla 2005 Alternator - Tested, 3-Month Warranty'. In the description, state condition, part number, compatible models, and your location. Price competitively but not too low. Respond to messages quickly; buyers often move to the next seller if you delay. Use WhatsApp Business to catalogue your parts and set up auto-replies. Join local buy-and-sell groups on Facebook and WhatsApp. Post daily or every other day, but don't spam. Offer delivery within your city for a small fee (e.g., 1,000 Naira or 100 KES). For distant buyers, use online payment methods like bank transfer or mobile money (M-Pesa, Airtel Money). Build trust by asking for reviews after each sale. A simple 'Thank you, please recommend me' goes a long way. Track which platforms bring the most sales. If Jiji works best, focus there. If mechanics buy more, visit them weekly. Consistency is key: market every day, even when you're busy with dismantling. Remember, a part not marketed is a part not sold.

lessons.title: Packaging and shipping parts to distant buyers
lessons.body: When you sell to a distant buyer, packaging and shipping must be done right to avoid damage and returns. Start with cleaning the part thoroughly; no one wants a greasy box. For small parts like alternators, starters, or ECUs, wrap them in bubble wrap or foam. If bubble wrap is expensive, use old newspaper or cardboard. Place the wrapped part in a sturdy cardboard box. Fill empty spaces with more newspaper, foam peanuts, or air pillows so the part doesn't move. For heavy parts like brake calipers or gearboxes, use a wooden crate or a double-walled box. Secure with strong tape (packing tape, not cello tape). Label the box clearly with the buyer's address and your return address. For shipping within your country, use bus companies (e.g., ABC Transport, Chisco in Nigeria; Easy Coach in Kenya) or courier services (G4S, DHL). Bus companies are cheaper for heavy items: a 10kg box might cost 2,000-3,000 Naira or 200-300 KES. Courier services are faster but pricier. For international shipping, use EMS, DHL, or FedEx, but check customs rules. Always insure high-value parts. Get a tracking number and share it with the buyer. Take photos of the packaged part before sealing and after sealing. This protects you if the buyer claims damage. For payment, insist on full payment before shipping. Use bank transfer or mobile money. If the buyer is new, ask for a deposit (50%) and the rest on delivery. For fragile parts like sensors, add 'FRAGILE' stickers. For liquids like brake fluid, don't ship; it's hazardous. After shipping, follow up with the buyer to confirm delivery. If they report damage, ask for photos and file a claim with the courier. Good packaging reduces returns and builds your reputation. A happy distant buyer will order again and refer others.

lessons.title: Offering warranties and handling returns professionally
lessons.body: Offering a warranty builds trust and can justify higher prices. But you must handle returns professionally to avoid losing money and reputation. Start with a simple written warranty: 30 days for rebuilt parts, 14 days for tested used parts, and no warranty for 'as-is' parts. Print warranty cards or write on the receipt: part name, date, warranty period, and your contact. Explain what is covered (defects in workmanship or part failure) and what is not (damage from installation error, overheating, or accidents). When a buyer returns a part, stay calm and polite. Ask for the receipt and the part. Inspect it immediately. If it's a valid warranty claim, offer a replacement, repair, or refund. For example, if a rebuilt alternator fails within 30 days, replace it or refund 100%. If the buyer damaged it, explain politely and offer a discount on a new part. Never argue; a bad review spreads fast. Keep a returns log: date, part, reason, action taken. This helps you spot patterns. If you see many returns for a certain part, stop selling it or improve your rebuild process. For refunds, use the same payment method. If you shipped the part, ask the buyer to ship it back; you can split shipping costs. For online sales, clearly state your return policy in the listing. Many platforms like Jiji allow buyers to rate you; a good rating means more sales. Consider offering a 'core charge' for rebuilt parts: you charge a deposit that is refunded when the buyer returns the old core. This ensures you get rebuildable cores. Finally, learn from every return. If a part fails, find out why. Was it a bad rebuild? Did you miss a crack? Improve your testing and rebuilding. A professional returns process turns a negative into a positive: the buyer sees you stand behind your work and becomes a loyal customer.

quiz.q: What is the first step before selling any used part?
quiz.explanation: Cleaning and testing ensure the part is functional and presentable, which increases its value and reduces returns.

quiz.q: Which tool is essential for testing alternators and starters?
quiz.explanation: A multimeter measures voltage and continuity, which are critical for testing electrical parts.

quiz.q: When testing an alternator by spinning the pulley, what voltage range should you expect?
quiz.explanation: A good alternator should produce around 12-14 volts DC when spun.

quiz.q: What should you do with a part that fails testing?
options: A) Sell it as a used part
C) Sell it as scrap metal
quiz.explanation: Failed parts can still be sold for their metal value, but not as functional used parts.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep a testing log?
options: B) To help price accurately and avoid returns
quiz.explanation: A testing log provides a record of each part's condition, which aids pricing and builds buyer trust.

quiz.q: What is a common failure in alternators that can be fixed with a rebuild kit?
quiz.explanation: Worn brushes are a common issue that rebuild kits address.

quiz.q: What tool is used to press out old bearings from an alternator?
quiz.explanation: A socket and hammer can be used to gently tap out bearings without damaging the housing.

quiz.q: What is the main problem that causes brake calipers to stick?
quiz.explanation: Rust on the piston prevents it from moving smoothly, causing the caliper to stick.

quiz.q: What should you use to clean a brake caliper bore?
options: B) Brake cleaner and a hone
quiz.explanation: Brake cleaner and a hone remove rust and debris without damaging the bore.

quiz.q: How much can a rebuilt alternator sell for in many African cities?
quiz.explanation: Rebuilt alternators often sell for 15,000-25,000 Naira or 1,000-1,500 KES depending on the market.

quiz.q: What grade would a used part that is like new, tested, and clean be?
quiz.explanation: Grade A parts are in excellent condition and command the highest prices.

quiz.q: What percentage of new price can a Grade A used part typically sell for?
quiz.explanation: Grade A parts are high quality and can fetch 50-70% of the new price.

quiz.q: Why do parts for popular models like Toyota sell faster?
options: C) They are easier to find
quiz.explanation: Popular models have more vehicles on the road, so demand for their parts is higher.

quiz.q: What is a good rule for pricing Grade A and B parts?
options: C) Never sell below cost plus 20%
quiz.explanation: To ensure profit, avoid selling below your cost plus a 20% margin for good parts.

quiz.q: What should you do if a part is not selling?
options: B) Lower the price to move it
quiz.explanation: Lowering the price can help clear inventory and free up space for faster-selling items.

quiz.q: What is a good way to market parts to local mechanics?
options: B) Visit them with a parts list and offer commission
quiz.explanation: Personal visits and commission incentives encourage mechanics to buy from you and refer others.

quiz.q: Which online platform is commonly used for selling used parts in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Jiji is a popular classifieds platform in many African countries for buying and selling used goods.

quiz.q: What should you include in an online listing for a part?
options: B) Clear photos, detailed description, and price
quiz.explanation: Clear photos and detailed descriptions help buyers understand the part and build trust.

quiz.q: Why is it important to respond quickly to online inquiries?
options: B) Buyers often move to the next seller if you delay
C) To increase your data usage
quiz.explanation: Fast responses increase the chance of closing a sale because buyers are often comparing multiple sellers.

quiz.q: What is a good way to build trust with online buyers?
options: A) Ask for reviews after each sale
quiz.explanation: Positive reviews from satisfied buyers enhance your reputation and attract more customers.

quiz.q: What should you use to protect small parts during shipping?
quiz.explanation: Bubble wrap or newspaper provides cushioning to prevent damage during transit.

quiz.q: Which shipping method is often cheaper for heavy parts within a country?
quiz.explanation: Bus companies like ABC Transport are cost-effective for heavy items within a country.

quiz.q: What should you do before sealing a package for shipping?
options: A) Take photos of the packaged part
quiz.explanation: Photos serve as evidence of the part's condition before shipping, protecting you from false damage claims.

quiz.q: Why should you insist on full payment before shipping?
quiz.explanation: Full payment upfront prevents buyers from refusing to pay after receiving the part.

quiz.q: What should you do if a buyer reports damage after shipping?
options: B) Ask for photos and file a claim with the courier
quiz.explanation: Photos help verify the damage, and filing a claim with the courier can recover your loss.

quiz.q: What is a typical warranty period for a rebuilt part?
quiz.explanation: A 30-day warranty is common for rebuilt parts, balancing buyer confidence and seller risk.

quiz.q: What should you do when a buyer returns a part under warranty?
options: B) Inspect it and offer replacement, repair, or refund
D) Keep the part and money
quiz.explanation: Professional handling of returns maintains trust and encourages repeat business.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep a returns log?
options: A) To spot patterns and improve
quiz.explanation: A returns log helps identify recurring issues and improve your rebuilding or testing process.

quiz.q: What is a 'core charge'?
options: A) A deposit refunded when the old part is returned
quiz.explanation: A core charge ensures you get the old part back for rebuilding, which is valuable.

quiz.q: How can a professional returns process benefit your business?
options: A) It turns a negative into a positive and builds loyalty
quiz.explanation: Handling returns well shows you stand behind your products, leading to customer loyalty and positive word-of-mouth.
